cohort: Mothers from the multisite Collaborative Perinatal Project (CPP) cohort (1959-1966; n=43,646) were included, limited to their last CPP delivery.
finding: Cesarean vs vaginal delivery was significantly associated with increased risk for all-cause mortality (HR=1.16) and increased risk of death from cardiovascular disease, diabetes, respiratory disease, infection, and kidney disease, while labor duration was not significantly related to overall mortality.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery, compared to vaginal delivery, was associated with an increased risk for subsequent all-cause and cause-specific mortality, particularly related to cardiovascular disease and diabetes.
